items.title: MBBS graduate moves Supreme Court for degree withheld by college after NIA seized fees she paid
items.summary: A peculiar case involving competing rights of an MBBS graduate, the medical college where she studied, and the National Investigation Agency (NIA) has reached the Supreme Court [Pooja Kumari Vs Union of India] The MBBS graduate has moved the apex court challenging the college's decision to withhold her degree and course completion certificate after the fees paid by her to the college was seized by NIA as part of investigation against some of her relatives. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta on Thursday issued notice to the Central government and the college on a plea by the graduate challenging the demand by the college that she pay her fees again to have her certificates released. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The student had secured admission to the MBBS course at Chettinad Academy of Research and Education in 2017 through the regular counselling process. Over the course of her studies, she paid ₹1.13 crore in fees to the college through banking channels and completed both the MBBS course and her compulsory rotating medical internship. In December 2021, the NIA registered a case under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against some of her relatives over alleged Maoist links. Her brother was also made an accused. The student herself was not arraigned as an accused. During the investigation, the NIA treated the money paid towards her college fees as alleged proceeds of crime and seized the amount from the college. Thereafter, the college refused to issue her final MBBS degree, provisional certificate-II and course completion certificate. It took the position that since the amount received by it had been seized by the NIA, the student would have to pay the entire fee again before the certificates could be released. The student challenged this before the Madras High Court, arguing that she had already paid the fees and could not be made to pay twice merely because the amount was subsequently seized by an investigating agency. items.title: J&K terror case: Delhi High Court grants bail to 2 UAPA accused who spent nearly 5 years in custody
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday granted bail to Sobiya Aziz and Kamran Ashraf Reshi, two accused in an Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) case alleging a wide-ranging terror conspiracy by banned outfits in Jammu and Kashmir [Kamran Ashraf Reshi v. National Investigation Agency] . A Division Bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Ravinder Dudeja held that both the accused had already suffered a custody of almost 5 years pending trial and there is no chance of the trial ending soon. “We have also minutely perused the allegations against the appellant Kamran Ashraf Reshi, as also the material relied upon by the NIA against him. While we refrain from giving a detailed account of the same, as we fear that it may prejudice the trial, we are of the opinion that given the long period of incarceration of the appellant juxtaposed against the material alleged against him by the NIA, the appellant has been able to make out a case for being released on bail,” the Court said in Reshi’s case. In Aziz’s case, the Bench observed that while the National Investigation Agency (NIA) said there is some prima facie material, she still has an arguable case for grant of bail. Justice Navin Chawla and Justice Ravinder Dudeja The NIA had alleged that there was a wide-ranging terror conspiracy involving proscribed organisations such as Lashkar-e-Taiba, Jaish-e-Mohammed, Hizb-ul-Mujahideen, Al Badr, The Resistance Front, People Against Fascist Forces, Mujahideen Gazwatul Hind etc active in Jammu & Kashmir and was being orchestrated from Pakistan. It was stated that these organisations are conspiring to undertake terror attacks in Kashmir and other cities of India and radicalising Indians. Aziz, arrested in October 2021, was accused of assisting active terrorists, including allegedly transporting a militant and possessing incriminating diaries and an Islamic State flag. Reshi was arrested at the age of 21 and accused of association with online propaganda groups and Pakistan-based handlers. After considering the case, the Court noted that out of 359 cited witnesses, only 21 had been examined, making early conclusion of the trial unlikely. The Bench also noted that several co-accused in the case were already granted bail and that Section 43D(5) of the UAPA does not oust constitutional courts' power to grant bail where prolonged incarceration and trial delay implicate Article 21 rights.
